guide_line: Build a configuration or an orbital-box diagram, including the chromium and copper exceptions.
steps: Orbitals fill in this order: 1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, 3d, 4p, 5s, 4d, 5p. An s subshell holds 2 electrons, a p holds 6, a d holds 10, and an f holds 14.
A noble-gas core stands for the finished inner orbitals. [He] is 1s2. [Ne] is 1s2 2s2 2p6. [Ar] is that plus 3s2 3p6. [Kr] adds 4s2 3d10 4p6.
An orbital-box diagram uses one box for each orbital. An arrow is one electron. In a subshell, give every box one electron before you pair any. Paired arrows in one box point opposite ways.
Chromium and copper break the usual order. Cr is [Ar] 4s1 3d5, not 4s2 3d4. Cu is [Ar] 4s1 3d10, not 4s2 3d9.
A cation loses electrons from the highest n first. Remove 4s before 3d. Fe2+ is [Ar] 3d6. Fe3+ is [Ar] 3d5. Cu+ is [Ar] 3d10.
To name the element from a configuration, add up the electrons. For a neutral atom, that sum is the atomic number.

worked_example.q: Write the electron configuration of iron (Fe). Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
steps: Iron has atomic number 26, so a neutral atom has 26 electrons.
The argon core accounts for 18. The next eight are 4s2 3d6.

similar_problem.q: A neutral atom has the configuration [Ar] 4s2 3d10 4p3. Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
similar_problem.hint: Argon is 18 electrons. Add 2 + 10 + 3 more, and match that atomic number to the symbol.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of carbon (C). Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Carbon has atomic number 6, so the neutral atom has 6 electrons. Filled in order, that is [He] 2s2 2p2.
hints: After 1s2 2s2, carbon still has two electrons. They go in 2p.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of oxygen (O). Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Oxygen has atomic number 8, so the neutral atom has 8 electrons. Filled in order, that is [He] 2s2 2p4.
hints: Oxygen has eight electrons. After 1s2 2s2, four electrons remain for 2p.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of sodium (Na). Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Sodium has atomic number 11, so the neutral atom has 11 electrons. Filled in order, that is [Ne] 3s1.
hints: Sodium has one electron past the neon core. That electron is in 3s.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of phosphorus (P). Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Phosphorus has atomic number 15, so the neutral atom has 15 electrons. Filled in order, that is [Ne] 3s2 3p3.
hints: Phosphorus is past neon. Put two electrons in 3s and the other three, unpaired, in 3p.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of calcium (Ca). Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Calcium has atomic number 20, so the neutral atom has 20 electrons. Filled in order, that is [Ar] 4s2.
hints: Calcium finishes argon and then fills 4s. The 3d subshell is still empty.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of iron (Fe). Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Iron has atomic number 26, so the neutral atom has 26 electrons. Filled in order, that is [Ar] 4s2 3d6.
hints: Iron finishes 4s and then places six electrons in 3d. Do not remove 4s for a neutral atom.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of chromium (Cr). Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Chromium has atomic number 24. The usual fill would end in 4s2 3d4. One 4s electron moves into 3d, so the configuration is [Ar] 4s1 3d5.
hints: Chromium does not stay at 4s2 3d4. Move one electron so 3d is half full.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of copper (Cu). Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Copper has atomic number 29. The usual fill would end in 4s2 3d9. One 4s electron moves into 3d, so the configuration is [Ar] 4s1 3d10.
hints: Copper does not stay at 4s2 3d9. Move one electron so 3d is full.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of bromine (Br). Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Bromine has atomic number 35, so the neutral atom has 35 electrons. Filled in order, that is [Ar] 4s2 3d10 4p5.
hints: Bromine is five electrons into 4p, after a full 3d and a full 4s.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of manganese (Mn). Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Manganese has atomic number 25, so the neutral atom has 25 electrons. Filled in order, that is [Ar] 4s2 3d5.
hints: Manganese has a half-full 3d subshell and a full 4s. It is not the chromium exception.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of zinc (Zn). Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Zinc has atomic number 30, so the neutral atom has 30 electrons. Filled in order, that is [Ar] 4s2 3d10.
hints: Zinc has a full 3d subshell and a full 4s. Both 4s electrons stay.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of Fe3+. Remove electrons from the highest n first. Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Start with neutral iron, [Ar] 4s2 3d6. Remove 3 electrons from the highest n first. Fe3+ is [Ar] 3d5.
hints: Start from neutral iron, then remove three electrons. Take both 4s electrons before any 3d electron.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of Cl-. Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Neutral chlorine is [Ne] 3s2 3p5. The added electron completes the open subshell. Cl- is [Ar].
hints: Chlorine's neutral atom ends in 3p5. The extra electron fills that 3p subshell.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of Cu+. Remove electrons from the highest n first. Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Start with neutral copper, [Ar] 4s1 3d10. Remove 1 electron from the highest n first. Cu+ is [Ar] 3d10.
hints: Start from copper's exception, [Ar] 4s1 3d10, then remove the 4s electron.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of Co2+. Remove electrons from the highest n first. Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Start with neutral cobalt, [Ar] 4s2 3d7. Remove 2 electrons from the highest n first. Co2+ is [Ar] 3d7.
hints: Neutral cobalt is [Ar] 4s2 3d7. A 2+ ion loses the two 4s electrons and keeps 3d7.

problems.q: A neutral atom has the configuration [Ne] 3s2 3p4. Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: The electrons add to 16. Atomic number 16 is S.
hints: Neon is 10. This configuration adds four electrons in 3p and two in 3s.

problems.q: A neutral atom has the configuration [Ne] 3s2 3p5. Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: The electrons add to 17. Atomic number 17 is Cl.
hints: The 3p subshell is one electron short of full. Count from neon, not from argon.

problems.q: A neutral atom has the configuration [Ar] 4s2 3d10 4p2. Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: The electrons add to 32. Atomic number 32 is Ge.
hints: Argon is 18. Add the 4s, 3d, and 4p electrons in this configuration.

problems.q: A neutral atom has the configuration [Ar] 4s1 3d5. Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: The electrons add to 24. Atomic number 24 is Cr.
hints: A 4s1 3d5 ending is the half-full exception. Add 1 + 5 to argon's 18.

problems.q: A neutral atom has the configuration [Ar] 4s1 3d10. Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: The electrons add to 29. Atomic number 29 is Cu.
hints: A 4s1 3d10 ending is the full-d exception. Add 1 + 10 to argon's 18.

problems.q: A neutral atom has the configuration [Ar] 4s2 3d10 4p6. Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: The electrons add to 36. Atomic number 36 is Kr.
hints: The 4p subshell is full. Adding those electrons to argon finishes the next noble gas.

problems.q: A neutral atom has the configuration [Kr] 5s2. Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: The electrons add to 38. Atomic number 38 is Sr.
hints: Krypton is 36 electrons. Two more electrons sit in 5s.

problems.q: A neutral atom has the configuration 1s2 2s2 2p3. Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: The electrons add to 7. Atomic number 7 is N.
hints: Add 2 + 2 + 3. There is no noble-gas core hiding extra electrons.

problems.q: A neutral atom has the configuration [Ar] 4s2 3d6. Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: The electrons add to 26. Atomic number 26 is Fe.
hints: Past argon, count two 4s electrons and six 3d electrons.

problems.q: A neutral atom has the configuration [Ar] 4s2 3d8. Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: The electrons add to 28. Atomic number 28 is Ni.
hints: This is two electrons past iron's 3d6. Keep both electrons in 4s.

problems.q: A neutral atom has the configuration [Kr] 5s2 4d10 5p5. Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: The electrons add to 53. Atomic number 53 is I.
hints: Krypton is 36. Add the 5s, 4d, and 5p electrons shown here.

problems.q: A neutral atom has the configuration [Ar] 4s2 3d10 4p3. Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: The electrons add to 33. Atomic number 33 is As.
hints: The 4p subshell is half full. Add 2 + 10 + 3 to argon's 18.

problems.q: An ion with charge 2+ has the configuration [Ar] 3d6. Write the ion symbol with a plain plus or hyphen, like Mg2+ or O2-.
problems.why: [Ar] 3d6 has 24 electrons. A 2+ ion has atomic number 26, so the symbol is Fe2+.
hints: The ion is 2+, and the configuration has no 4s electrons. Add 6 to argon, then add the 2 lost electrons to get the atomic number.

problems.q: An ion with charge 3+ has the configuration [Ar] 3d5. Write the ion symbol with a plain plus or hyphen, like Mg2+ or O2-.
problems.why: [Ar] 3d5 has 23 electrons. A 3+ ion has atomic number 26, so the symbol is Fe3+.
hints: A 3+ charge means three more protons than electrons. The configuration shows 18 + 5 electrons.

problems.q: An ion with charge 1+ has the configuration [Ar] 3d10. Write the ion symbol with a plain plus or hyphen, like Mg2+ or O2-.
problems.why: [Ar] 3d10 has 28 electrons. A 1+ ion has atomic number 29, so the symbol is Cu+.
hints: A 1+ ion with a full 3d and no 4s electron is one proton past the electron count.

problems.q: How many unpaired electrons does a neutral oxygen atom have? Type the number only.
problems.why: Oxygen is [He] 2s2 2p4. Placing those electrons by Hund's rule leaves 2 unpaired.
hints: In oxygen, the 2p subshell has four electrons and three orbitals. Two electrons are paired and two are alone.

problems.q: How many unpaired electrons does a neutral nitrogen atom have? Type the number only.
problems.why: Nitrogen is [He] 2s2 2p3. Placing those electrons by Hund's rule leaves 3 unpaired.
hints: Nitrogen's 2p subshell has three electrons in three orbitals. Hund's rule leaves all three unpaired.

problems.q: How many unpaired electrons does a neutral iron atom have? Type the number only.
problems.why: Iron is [Ar] 4s2 3d6. Placing those electrons by Hund's rule leaves 4 unpaired.
hints: Neutral iron is 4s2 3d6. The 4s electrons are paired. Count the singles left in 3d.

problems.q: How many unpaired electrons does a neutral chromium atom have? Type the number only.
problems.why: Chromium is [Ar] 4s1 3d5. Placing those electrons by Hund's rule leaves 6 unpaired.
hints: Use chromium's real configuration, 4s1 3d5. Every one of those six electrons is unpaired.

problems.q: How many unpaired electrons does a neutral copper atom have? Type the number only.
problems.why: Copper is [Ar] 4s1 3d10. Placing those electrons by Hund's rule leaves 1 unpaired.
hints: Use copper's real configuration, 4s1 3d10. The 3d subshell is full, so only the 4s electron is unpaired.

problems.q: How many unpaired electrons does a neutral zinc atom have? Type the number only.
problems.why: Zinc is [Ar] 4s2 3d10. Placing those electrons by Hund's rule leaves 0 unpaired.
hints: Zinc is 4s2 3d10. Both subshells are full, so every electron has a partner.

problems.q: How many valence electrons does neutral sulfur have? Type the number only.
problems.why: Sulfur is [Ne] 3s2 3p4. The electrons in the highest n add to 6.
hints: Sulfur's highest shell is n = 3. Add the 3s and 3p electrons, and do not count the neon core.

problems.q: How many valence electrons does neutral calcium have? Type the number only.
problems.why: Calcium is [Ar] 4s2. The electrons in the highest n add to 2.
hints: Calcium's highest shell is n = 4, and only the 4s electrons are in it.

problems.q: How many valence electrons does neutral bromine have? Type the number only.
problems.why: Bromine is [Ar] 4s2 3d10 4p5. The electrons in the highest n add to 7.
hints: Bromine's highest shell is n = 4. Count 4s and 4p. Leave the 3d electrons out of the valence count.

problems.q: Type the orbital-box diagram for neutral oxygen. Include every occupied subshell from 1s through 2p. Use ↑ and ↓, one space between orbitals, [] for an empty orbital, and | between subshells. Unpaired arrows are ↑. A filled orbital is written ↑↓.
problems.why: Oxygen is [He] 2s2 2p4. Drawing every occupied subshell with one arrow in each orbital before pairing gives 1s ↑↓ | 2s ↑↓ | 2p ↑↓ ↑ ↑.
hints: Oxygen has four 2p electrons. Pair the first 2p orbital only after each 2p orbital has one arrow.

problems.q: Type the orbital-box diagram for neutral nitrogen. Include every occupied subshell from 1s through 2p. Use ↑ and ↓, one space between orbitals, [] for an empty orbital, and | between subshells. Unpaired arrows are ↑. A filled orbital is written ↑↓.
problems.why: Nitrogen is [He] 2s2 2p3. Drawing every occupied subshell with one arrow in each orbital before pairing gives 1s ↑↓ | 2s ↑↓ | 2p ↑ ↑ ↑.
hints: Nitrogen has three 2p electrons. Draw three 2p arrows in three different orbitals, all pointing up.

problems.q: Type the orbital-box diagram for neutral carbon. Include every occupied subshell from 1s through 2p. Use ↑ and ↓, one space between orbitals, [] for an empty orbital, and | between subshells. Unpaired arrows are ↑. A filled orbital is written ↑↓.
problems.why: Carbon is [He] 2s2 2p2. Drawing every occupied subshell with one arrow in each orbital before pairing gives 1s ↑↓ | 2s ↑↓ | 2p ↑ ↑ [].
hints: Carbon has two 2p electrons. Show the empty 2p orbital as [] instead of pairing the two arrows.

problems.q: Type the orbital-box diagram for neutral chromium. Show only the 4s and 3d orbitals. Use ↑ and ↓, one space between orbitals, [] for an empty orbital, and | between subshells. Unpaired arrows are ↑. A filled orbital is written ↑↓.
problems.why: Chromium is [Ar] 4s1 3d5. Drawing only 4s and 3d with one arrow in each orbital before pairing gives 4s ↑ | 3d ↑ ↑ ↑ ↑ ↑.
hints: Draw chromium's exception, not 4s2 3d4. One 4s arrow and five separate 3d arrows.

problems.q: Type the orbital-box diagram for neutral copper. Show only the 4s and 3d orbitals. Use ↑ and ↓, one space between orbitals, [] for an empty orbital, and | between subshells. Unpaired arrows are ↑. A filled orbital is written ↑↓.
problems.why: Copper is [Ar] 4s1 3d10. Drawing only 4s and 3d with one arrow in each orbital before pairing gives 4s ↑ | 3d ↑↓ ↑↓ ↑↓ ↑↓ ↑↓.
hints: Draw copper's exception, not 4s2 3d9. One 4s arrow, and every 3d orbital paired.

problems.q: This orbital-box diagram is 1s ↑↓ | 2s ↑↓ | 2p ↑↓ ↑ ↑. Write the electron configuration. Separate orbitals with spaces, like 1s2 2s2 2p6. A noble-gas core such as [Ne] is also fine.
problems.why: Each ↑↓ is two electrons and each single ↑ is one. The diagram has 1s2 2s2 2p4, which is [He] 2s2 2p4.
hints: Count the arrows in each labeled subshell. Two arrows in one orbital count as 2.

problems.q: This orbital-box diagram belongs to a neutral atom: 1s ↑↓ | 2s ↑↓ | 2p ↑ ↑ ↑. Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: The arrows add to 7 electrons. Atomic number 7 is N.
hints: Add every arrow. A neutral atom with that many electrons has that atomic number.

problems.q: These are the outer boxes of a neutral atom: 4s ↑ | 3d ↑ ↑ ↑ ↑ ↑. The core is argon. Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: One 4s arrow and five 3d arrows are 6 electrons past argon's 18. Atomic number 24 is Cr.
hints: Count the outer arrows and add them to 18. The single 4s arrow is the chromium pattern.
